review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: Ὅλως ἀκούεται ἐν ὑμῖν πορνεία, καὶ τοιαύτη πορνεία ἥτις οὐδὲ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, ὥστε γυναῖκά τινα τοῦ πατρὸς ἔχειν.
5:1.targetText: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is intolerable even among pagans: A man has his father’s wife.

groups.note: The passive ἀκούεται ("is heard") is rendered It is reported.
τοιαύτη ("such") is rendered of a kind.
οὐδέ ("not even") is rendered intolerable even; the negative is carried by intolerable.
τινα ("someone") is rendered A man.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat sexual immorality here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB uses a colon instead of rendering ὥστε ("so that").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a clause frame; in the Greek πορνεία is the subject of ἀκούεται.
English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

5:2.sourceText: καὶ ὑμεῖς πεφυσιωμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἐπενθήσατε, ἵνα ἀρθῇ ἐκ μέσου ὑμῶν ὁ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο πράξας;
5:2.targetText: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have been stricken with grief and have removed from your fellowship the man who did this?

groups.note: The perfect participle πεφυσιωμένοι ("puffed up") is rendered proud.
οὐχί … ἐπενθήσατε ("did you not mourn") is rendered Shouldn’t you have been stricken with grief; the negative shares the contraction with the verb.
ἵνα ("so that") is rendered and.
The passive ἀρθῇ ("might be taken away") is rendered with the active have removed.
μέσου ("midst") is rendered fellowship.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new question instead of rendering καί ("and").
BSB renders τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο ("this deed") as this alone.

5:3.sourceText: ἐγὼ μὲν γάρ, ἀπὼν τῷ σώματι παρὼν δὲ τῷ πνεύματι, ἤδη κέκρικα ὡς παρὼν τὸν οὕτως τοῦτο κατεργασάμενον
5:3.targetText: Although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did this, just as if I were present.

groups.note: ἐγώ is the subject of κέκρικα and of each participle; BSB repeats I in each clause.
μέν … δέ ("on the one hand … but") is rendered by Although.
κέκρικα ("I have judged") is rendered have pronounced judgment on.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render γάρ ("for").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render οὕτως ("in this way").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies from you; the Greek has only ἀπών ("being absent").
English supplies with you; the Greek has only παρών ("being present").
English joins the clauses; the Greek has no καί here.

5:4.sourceText: ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ συναχθέντων ὑμῶν καὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ πνεύματος σὺν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ,
5:4.targetText: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, along with the power of the Lord Jesus,

groups.note: ἐμοῦ ("my") is rendered I; BSB recasts my spirit as I … in spirit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ἡμῶν ("our") with the second Lord.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.
English supplies a verb for the second subject; the Greek shares the participle συναχθέντων.

5:5.sourceText: παραδοῦναι τὸν τοιοῦτον τῷ Σατανᾷ εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκός, ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα σωθῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου.
5:5.targetText: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.

groups.note: τοιοῦτον ("such a one") is rendered this man.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:6.sourceText: Οὐ καλὸν τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν. οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ;
5:6.targetText: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough?

groups.note: ζυμοῖ ("leavens") is rendered works through.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

5:7.sourceText: ἐκκαθάρατε τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα, καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι. καὶ γὰρ τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός.
5:7.targetText: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

groups.note: ἐκκαθάρατε ("clean out") is rendered Get rid of.
ἄζυμοι ("unleavened"), the complement of ἐστε, is placed by BSB before batch.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders καὶ γάρ ("for also") with For alone.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds emphasis; the Greek has only ἐστε ("you are").

5:8.sourceText: ὥστε ἑορτάζωμεν, μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας καὶ πονηρίας, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινίας καὶ ἀληθείας.
5:8.targetText: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth.

groups.note: ἑορτάζωμεν ("let us celebrate the feast") is one verb.
ζύμῃ ("with leaven") is rendered leavened.
The genitive κακίας ("of malice") is rendered with malice after leavened.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB gives this ζύμῃ ("leaven") no word of its own: it says the old bread and renders leaven once, as leavened.
BSB joins the second phrase to the first and does not render μηδὲ ἐν ("nor with").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies bread, as in unleavened bread later in the verse; the Greek here has ζύμῃ ("leaven").

5:9.sourceText: Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι πόρνοις,
5:9.targetText: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

5:10.sourceText: οὐ πάντως τοῖς πόρνοις τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἢ τοῖς πλεονέκταις καὶ ἅρπαξιν ἢ εἰδωλολάτραις, ἐπεὶ ὠφείλετε ἄρα ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελθεῖν.
5:10.targetText: I was not including the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.

groups.note: ἐπεὶ … ἄρα ("since then") is rendered In that case.
ὠφείλετε ("you were obliged") is rendered you would have.
ἐξελθεῖν ἐκ ("to go out of") is rendered to leave.
The article is rendered this, referring back to this world.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render πάντως ("altogether") as a separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject and auxiliary of including; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies the verb; the Greek clause has no verb and continues the instruction of 5:9.

5:11.sourceText: νῦν δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι ἐάν τις ἀδελφὸς ὀνομαζόμενος ᾖ πόρνος ἢ πλεονέκτης ἢ εἰδωλολάτρης ἢ λοίδορος ἢ μέθυσος ἢ ἅρπαξ, τῷ τοιούτῳ μηδὲ συνεσθίειν.
5:11.targetText: But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.

groups.note: ἔγραψα ("I wrote") is rendered I am writing.
ἐάν τις ("if anyone") is rendered anyone who.
ὀνομαζόμενος ("being called") is rendered claims to be.
συνεσθίειν ("to eat with") is rendered eat; BSB places With before such a man.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB uses a comma for this ἤ ("or").
BSB uses a comma for this ἤ ("or").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a contrast; the Greek has no connective here.

5:12.sourceText: τί γάρ μοι τοὺς ἔξω κρίνειν; οὐχὶ τοὺς ἔσω ὑμεῖς κρίνετε;
5:12.targetText: What business of mine is it to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?

groups.note: μοι ("to me") is rendered of mine.
κρίνετε ("do you judge") is rendered Are … to judge.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render γάρ ("for").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a noun; the Greek has τί μοι ("what to me").
English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies what they are outside; the Greek has only ἔξω ("outside").

5:13.sourceText: τοὺς δὲ ἔξω ὁ Θεὸς κρινεῖ. ἐξάρατε τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν.
5:13.targetText: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked man from among you.”

groups.note: ἐξ ("out of") is rendered from among.
ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ("yourselves") is rendered you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ ("but").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
